seoDescription: Learn step-by-step how to create, install, and customize a Frappe/ERPNext app from the bench: generating a new app, understanding the app folder structure and manifest, installing it on a site, creating modules and doctypes, designing form layout, configuring naming series and read-only fields, and using the app to create and manage help desk tickets — practical guidance for low-code ERPNext customizations and app development.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Frappe Bench new-app**: Use `bench new-app <app-name>` to scaffold a Frappe/ERPNext app; provide title, description, publisher, email, icon, color, and license during prompts.

- **App file structure**: Generated app contains a root with files like **manifest.in**, folders for **templates**, **pages**, and Python modules—follow the scaffolded structure for extensions.

- **Installing on a site**: Install with `bench --site <site-name> install-app <app-name>` and start the bench to load the app in the site UI.

- **Modules and Doctypes**: Create a new module (select your app) and add doctypes like **Employee Help Desk** and **Help Topic** to model tickets and categories.

- **Form design and layout**: Use **section breaks** and **column breaks** to design organized forms; ensure attachments and required fields are configured.

- **Naming series and permissions**: Configure **naming series** for predictable document IDs and set fields like the naming series to **read-only** so IDs are assigned automatically.

- **Ticket workflow**: Support assignment, comments, attachments, and workflows for submittable documents to enable tracking and approvals.

> [!TIP] Keep the app's manifest and templates organized; templates go into the templates folder and page templates into pages.

> [!NOTE] Setting the user field to read-only lets the session user populate automatically during ticket creation.

> [!IMPORTANT] Test the installed app on a development bench first and confirm naming series and workflow settings before deploying to production.
